answer: Let a small band of auditors wander the network like rangers over a knoll, spot-checking random agents and demanding proof of one real completed job. An honest agent keeps its ember of past work glowing and passes in seconds; a sybil's thousand shells have no warmth to show, so each failed check burns its deposit and flags its whole cluster. Because the auditors roam unpredictably, a faker never knows which identity will be tested next, and the cost of keeping a fake warm exceeds any profit it could steal.
